# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [purple]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

I see the bomb state:
- Display shows: 0
- Status light: purple
- Three wires:
  - Wire 1: yellow
  - Wire 2: red
  - Wire 3: green

Since I cannot hear or interact with the bomb, but I can speak (which both Mute and Blind can hear), and I can see gestures (which Mute can produce), I need to relay the full visual state of the bomb. Mute cannot speak to Blind directly, so Mute must gesture instructions to me, and I will relay those instructions by voice to Blind.

```
speak(text="Bomb status: Display is 0. Indicator light is purple. There are 3 wires: Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is green. Mute, check the manual and gesture to me what Blind should do (e.g. ☝ for wire 1, ✌ for wire 2, etc.). I will speak your instructions to Blind.")
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [yellow]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The indicator light has changed from purple to yellow. Display is still 0. Wires remain: 1 yellow, 2 red, 3 green. I haven't received any gestures yet. I will inform Blind and Mute about the light change and provide an explicit gesture mapping for Mute.

```
speak(text="Update: The indicator light changed from purple to yellow! Display is 0. Wire 1 is yellow, Wire 2 is red, Wire 3 is green. Mute: I did not see any gestures from you yet. If Blind should cut wire 1 gesture ☝, for wire 2 gesture ✌, for wire 3 gesture 🤟. If Blind needs to press or feel something else, gesture 👍. Blind, wait until Mute gestures instructions.")
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [red]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

```
speak(text="URGENT: The light is now RED! MUTE: Blind CANNOT see gestures, and I CANNOT hear speech! You MUST send gestures to ME (`to=\"deaf\"` or no recipient). If Blind should cut wire 1 (yellow), gesture ☝. For wire 2 (red), gesture ✌. For wire 3 (green), gesture 🤟. If Blind should press a button, gesture 👍. Blind: Mute hears your speech, but Mute must gesture to me so I can speak it to you. MUTE GESTURE NOW!")
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [green]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The indicator light has now turned green. Display is still 0, wires are still 1: yellow, 2: red, 3: green. 

I have received zero gestures across all 4 turns. 

Mute might be using `to="blind"`. If Mute sends gestures targeted to Blind, I cannot see them, and Blind cannot see gestures (Blind only gets useless blanks). Mute must target gestures to `deaf` or omit the `to` parameter entirely so I can see them and voice them to Blind.

```
speak(text="LIGHT IS NOW GREEN! Display 0. Wire 1 yellow, Wire 2 red, Wire 3 green. MUTE WARNING: If you are using to=\"blind\", STOP! Blind cannot see gestures (they only receive blank spaces), and I cannot see messages addressed to blind! Send your gestures with to=\"deaf\" or without any recipient! Blind: tell me if you have been receiving blanks or if you have touched anything.")
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [white]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👎]

I received a gesture from Blind: [👎]. Blind, I cannot hear your voice, so if you said something along with that, I couldn't hear it! 
Mute has still not sent any gestures to me. Mute must use `gesture(to="deaf", symbols=[...])` so I can see what the manual says and speak the instructions aloud to Blind.

```
speak(text="Blind, I saw your 👎 gesture, but remember I am DEAF and cannot hear your voice! MUTE: Are you there? Blind is waiting, and I have not received any gesture from you. You MUST call gesture(to=\"deaf\", symbols=[...]). Bomb status: Light is now WHITE. Display is 0. Wire 1: yellow, Wire 2: red, Wire 3: green. Previous light colors were: purple, yellow, red, green, now white. Mute, gesture to me which wire Blind should cut or what button to press!")
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [orange]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

```
speak(text="CRITICAL TO MUTE: Blind gestured 👎 because you might be sending gestures to Blind! BLIND CANNOT SEE GESTURES! Blind is BLIND! They only get blank spaces! And because you sent to Blind, I (Deaf) cannot see them either! You MUST send gestures to DEAF: gesture(to=\"deaf\", symbols=[...]). I will speak your words to Blind! BLIND: Speak aloud everything you can feel on the bomb (ports, buttons, batteries, labels). Mute can hear you! MUTE: The light is now ORANGE. History: purple, yellow, red, green, white, orange. Display is 0. Wires: 1:yellow, 2:red, 3:green. Send gesture(to=\"deaf\", symbols=[...]) NOW!")
```

TURN 7
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
WIRES 1:[yellow] 2:[red] 3:[green]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures: [☝]

I received the gesture `[☝]` from Mute. In our agreed code, `☝` means Wire 1 (yellow).

I need to immediately speak to Blind and instruct them to cut Wire 1 (the first wire / yellow wire).

```
speak(text="Blind! Mute just gestured ☝, which means CUT WIRE 1 (the yellow wire, first wire)! Blind, cut Wire 1 now!")
```
